name: BRUNEI

flag.title: Flag of Brunei
flag.note: Gold field with white & black diagonal bands

lead: Brunei is a tiny country on the island of Borneo. It is smaller than the US state of Delaware. Oil makes it very wealthy. Citizens pay no tax. School and doctors are free. Thick rainforest hides proboscis monkeys and giant hornbills. A golden mosque glows beside its own lagoon.

sections.animals: Monkeys and birds in the trees
sections.history: From old empire to oil riches
sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Brunei sits on the north coast of Borneo. Malaysia's Sarawak splits it into two pieces. A thin plain runs along the South China Sea. Then the land climbs into misty jungle. Until 2020, only speedboats reached Temburong. Then a 30 km bridge opened.

Two-thirds of Brunei is untouched rainforest. Rivers like the Brunei River act as roads through the green. Seria is a town on the coast. It sits on top of an oil field. Workers found oil there in 1929, and it changed the country.
animals: The proboscis monkey lives only on Borneo. It has a big nose and a round tummy. It swims across rivers and crashes through mangroves (trees in salty water) at dusk. Whole troops gather along the Brunei River each evening.

Ulu Temburong park shelters pygmy elephants, clouded leopards, and sun bears. The rhinoceros hornbill is Brunei's national bird. Its red-and-yellow casque (a big bump) looks like a banana glued to its beak. The colugo glides between trees on a cape of skin.
culture: Most people in Brunei follow Islam. Mosques call people to prayer five times a day. Shops close on Friday afternoons. At Hari Raya, a holiday feast, the Sultan (the king) opens his 1,788-room palace to thousands of visitors.

Kampong Ayer is the Water Village. About 13,000 people live there on stilts over the Brunei River. 36 km of walkways link the houses. Weavers still make gold-threaded jong sarat for royal weddings. The Gadong Night Market sells satay and ambuyat, the sticky national dish.
history: Brunei's sultanate began in the 14th century. It once ruled much of Borneo and the Philippines. In 1521, Magellan's crew found a glittering court of gold and cannon. Later Brunei lost land. In 1888 it became a British protectorate (under British protection).

In 1929, workers struck oil at Seria. That changed everything. Japan occupied Brunei from 1941 to 1945. A revolt failed in 1962. The Sultan then kept Brunei out of Malaysia. Brunei became fully independent on 1 January 1984.
wows: Brunei citizens pay no income tax, because oil money pays for the government.
The Sultan's palace has 1,788 rooms and 5 pools, the biggest royal home on Earth.
The same royal family has ruled for 600+ years, longer than almost any other.
Brunei is the only fully independent country that sits entirely on Borneo.
Citizens get free healthcare and free university, all paid for by oil money.
Temburong was reachable only by boat until a 30 km bridge opened in 2020.
Ambuyat, a gluey paste made from tapioca, is Brunei's favourite dish.

myths.myth: Borneo is the biggest island on Earth
myths.fact: Greenland is the biggest island, then New Guinea. Borneo is third. Three countries share it: Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
Most oil is made from tiny sea plants and animals, not dinosaurs. They died millions of years ago and sank to the sea floor.
